name: Aurora-Vault
description: Aurora-Vault earns its name twice over: its magnetic pole wanders a full circle every local year, dragging curtains of green and violet light across the entire sky in slow procession, while beneath the ice lies a dark ocean sealed like a held breath. The surface is glacier-smooth to the horizon, fractured only by pressure ridges that glow faint blue where fresh water freezes into the cracks.

Standing on the ice you hear two worlds at once—the thin wind above, and below your boots, faint but unmistakable, the tidal breathing of the buried ocean against its ceiling. In the crystal caverns where the shell thins, headlamp light fractures into cathedral colors, and the cold feels less like absence than architecture.

Microbial mats thrive in the subglacial sea, feeding the long argument about whether life here arose independently. The quarantine zone complicates everything: ground-penetrating radar shows a geometric structure buried under eleven kilometers of glacier at the pole—a lattice spanning four hundred kilometers, older than the ice sheet itself, humming with exotic matter signatures. No government has claimed it; all of them patrol it.

Dark crystal harvests from the caverns are already the sector's richest, and the lattice's exotic matter readings dwarf them. Three expeditions have drilled toward the structure without authorization; the ice closed behind each one, cleanly, within days. The microbes in the ocean, meanwhile, have begun organizing into rings—centered precisely beneath the pole.
